title: ID Card Printer
brief: Print a tidy ID card straight to the terminal. No input, no maths, just careful printing: the border, the labels lined up with tabs, and a quote with real quotation marks in it.

problem.goal: Write a program that prints a six line ID card: a border line, a name line, a role line, a language line, a quote line, and a closing border line.
rules: The first and last lines must each be exactly 25 equals signs.
The four middle lines must start with Name:, Role:, Language: and Motto: and use a tab after the colon.
The Motto line must have real double quotation marks around the motto text.
Put your own name on the Name line. Everything else can match the example.

steps: Line 1: print 25 equals signs. Count them, or copy the one in the example.
Lines 2 to 4: print each label, a tab, then the value. The tab is `\t`.
Line 5: print the Motto line. The quotation marks around the motto need escaping as `\"`.
Line 6: print the same border as line 1.
Press Run to see your card, then press Check Project to have it tested.
hints: Start with one line. Add `System.out.println("=========================");` and press Run. If a border appears, your program works and the rest is more of the same.
A tab is written `\t` inside the quotes. `System.out.println("Name:\tAmara");` prints Name: then a tab then Amara, all on one line.
Each line of the card is its own `System.out.println`. Six lines of output means six instructions, in the order you want them to appear.
For the Motto line, a quotation mark inside text has to be escaped with a backslash: `\"`. So the whole instruction is `System.out.println("Motto:\t\"I read my errors.\"");`
If the borders come out different lengths, count the equals signs. It is easier to write the first border, then copy that whole instruction and paste it at the end.
inputHint: This program asks no questions, so leave this empty and just press Run.

tests.name: The labels are lined up with tabs
The motto keeps its quotation marks

successMessage: Your ID card prints perfectly! 🪪 You wrote a class, a main method, six instructions in the right order, and you escaped a quotation mark inside a piece of text. That is Module 1 finished: next up, storing values in variables.
